editorial.headline: The Hidden Craft Behind Finished Print
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 18120 covers the prepress, binding, plate-making and finishing work that turns print materials into usable objects.
editorial.body:
KBLI 18120 is not the act of printing itself, but the specialised support work that makes printing possible and presentable. The record describes prepress and premedia services, binding, and related finishing services. In practical terms, this is the craft and technical layer between a design file, a printing process, and the finished printed object: books, brochures, magazines, catalogues and other printed materials that need to be folded, assembled, stitched, glued, trimmed, bound or finished with details such as gold stamping.

The scope is deliberately broad because printing support is both physical and digital. It includes composing, typesetting, photographic typesetting, and entering prepress data into forms usable across printing processes and other visual media. It also includes scanning, optical character recognition, and electronic assembly. The same activity can prepare data files for multimedia applications across paper printing, CD-ROM and internet use. On the production side, it reaches into plate-making, image and plate arrangement for press and offset processes, cylinder preparation for gravure through engraving or etching, computer-to-plate processing including photopolymer plates, and preparation of plates or forms for relief printing and stamping.

That breadth explains who may register it. The slim record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so it is not reserved only for large industrial operators. A small bindery, a prepress studio, a plate-preparation service, or a larger post-print finishing operation can all sit within the same activity when the work matches the recorded scope. The common thread is that the business supports printing through preparation, technical artwork, proof-making, binding, finishing, sample mounting or related post-print services, rather than being defined by a single product category.

The national investment picture is clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, with the cited source listed as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali does not change that into a local closure in this record. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. The stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium still matters as context because the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. But for this activity, the record’s own Bali conclusion is that it is not blocked by that moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is that KBLI 18120 is nationally foreign-open and, on this record, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
